question: The Thessaloniki International Fair (TIF) is currently held in Thessaloniki city centre. Since 1985, the master plan and the general urban development plan have envisaged the creation of a metropolitan park at the current site of the Thessaloniki International Fair and the relocation of the fair to the western part of the city with a view to improving quality of life and stimulating growth.

The project is now being scrapped from the government-backed TIF ‘redevelopment’ plan, in favour of an old redevelopment plan that involves building a shopping centre and hotel at the current location as part of a public-private partnership, with the state guaranteeing profits for investors.

Although the proposed redevelopment plan goes against greening and resilience goals, it is to receive EU funding according to government statements. Seven mayors from west Thessaloniki have expressed their objections to the planning in writing, saying they support the relocation plan and the creation of the metropolitan park on the current TIF site.

West Thessaloniki and the surrounding area are economically and socially deprived parts of the city affected by environmental degradation. Relocating the TIF will be a strategic investment that will boost sustainable, green and balanced growth, particularly in the western part of the city where there is deprivation due to unemployment and a lack of infrastructure.

In view of this: What will the Commission do about the fact that public and European money is to be used to fund a project that runs counter to sustainable development and an improved quality of life and will thus have a negative impact on the centre and suburbs of Thessaloniki?
answer: EN E-1167/2024 on behalf of the European Commission (20.6.2024) With regard to the question of the Honourable Member of the European Parliament, the Commission services are not aware of any action financed under the Cohesion Policy related to the relocation of the International Fair of Thessalonica. Also, there is no action financed under the Recovery and Resilience Facility devoted to this.
